I have been working this land for 50 years. My body is older now — 74 is not 40 — and there are only two of us in the house. I do not take chances. I do what I know works.

For wheat, I will sow around October 10th on all 3 mu, same as always. I use an improved variety — Ji Mai series, what the village seed shop carries, nothing experimental. I hire a machine for rotary tillage before seeding; I cannot manage deep ploughing anymore and honestly rotary has served me fine for years. I put down compound fertilizer at planting, then chase with urea at jointing. Nitrogen around 15 jin per mu — I know some younger farmers go heavier but I have seen burning and waste. Hebei is dry so I will water four times: before winter sets in, at jointing, at heading, and at grain filling. I spray herbicide early and watch for aphids closer to heading. I expect around 450 jin per mu. That is honest and steady.

For maize, I seed straight into the wheat stubble after harvest in mid-June — no tillage needed, saves my back and saves diesel money. I use hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or whatever is available locally that year, the hybrid is not a question anymore for anyone here. I apply fertilizer twice — base at seeding, chase with urea at the big bell stage. Summer has rain but I will water twice if it is dry at tasseling and filling — the well is there for a reason. Two sprays: one herbicide pass early, one for corn borer if I see it. I expect around 550 jin per mu.

Three mu total, two crops in sequence, same field. This feeds us and gives a small surplus to sell.
